non_applicability_conditions: Findings characterize only the eight sources the published /e2e-automation survey itself cites (citation manifest sha256:8a706a96500fcd8177ed048f4a81ac605fa5aabc67cea7b5fe1ef1e90855691b). They say nothing about the state of end-to-end research automation as a field, and nothing about work the survey did not cite.

Classification rests on abstracts only (content snapshot sha256:44671835a6e9c02e4e5d72aff20f4b57cb35aa07ef678e076f6e2a6debe9b1db). An abstract may understate or overstate a paper's own contribution; a full-text reading could move an individual row.

The strict first-stage criterion in end-to-end-research-automation-v1 (the system must not be handed the research idea) is a local operationalization. Under a looser reading of 'end-to-end', rows classified as qualifies would move toward supports.
A source's classification here is about what it CONTRIBUTES, never a judgement of its quality or importance.

conditions: a source must be cited by the published survey itself, not merely related to its subject
classification is made against the source's own abstract, never against the survey's characterisation of it
an abstract that does not settle the question is recorded unverifiable, never guessed
scope_of_validity.population: every citation in the pinned citation manifest of the published /e2e-automation survey (corpora/e2e-survey/citations.manifest.json, sha256:8a706a96500fcd8177ed048f4a81ac605fa5aabc67cea7b5fe1ef1e90855691b, 8 citations), classified against the pinned abstract snapshot fetched for them (corpora/e2e-survey/verification/content-snapshot.json, sha256:44671835a6e9c02e4e5d72aff20f4b57cb35aa07ef678e076f6e2a6debe9b1db, 8 of 8 abstracts available)
